epochsmith.configuration.title: Epochsmith Configs
era.epochsmith.entered: A new age of invention begins
chronicle.epochsmith.title: Chronicle of Invention
chronicle.epochsmith.contents_hint: Turn the page to read each chapter. New chapters reveal themselves as you invent.
chronicle.epochsmith.locked_first: Pick up a piece of flint to begin your journey.
chronicle.epochsmith.locked: Build the %s to reveal this chapter.
chronicle.epochsmith.primitive.intro: For most of history, tools were shaped by hand. Early people knapped flint into sharp edges, tamed fire, and fired clay into pots.
chronicle.epochsmith.bronze_iron.intro: Around 3300 BCE, smiths found that copper mixed with tin makes bronze. Later, the bloomery furnace let them smelt iron.
chronicle.epochsmith.mechanical.intro: Engineers put water and wind to work. Wheels ground grain, and geared devices like the ancient Greek Antikythera mechanism tracked the sky.
chronicle.epochsmith.industrial.intro: In the 1700s, steam engines turned coal into motion. Factories, railways and cheap steel soon followed.
chronicle.epochsmith.electrical.intro: In the 1800s, dynamos made electricity on demand. The telegraph carried messages, and electric bulbs lit homes.
chronicle.epochsmith.information.intro: The transistor, invented in 1947, made computers small and cheap. Circuits, software and networks followed.
chronicle.epochsmith.future.intro: No one knows what comes next. This chapter imagines ideas scientists work on today, like fusion power. A glimpse, not a prediction.
